title: Binary Tree Traversal Orders
statement:
Return preorder, inorder, and postorder value lists for one binary tree.

Contract
- `root` may be null.
- Return a `TraversalOrders` record containing the three lists.
- Empty trees produce three empty lists and the tree must not be mutated.

Examples
- `[1, 2, 3, null, 4]` yields preorder `[1, 2, 4, 3]`, inorder `[2, 4, 1, 3]`, and postorder `[4, 2, 3, 1]`.
- `[7]` yields `[7]` for all three orders.
hints: Preorder records the node before its children.
Inorder records left subtree, node, then right subtree; postorder records children before the node.
Append to three output lists at the right moments during one traversal. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output space.
inputSyntax: Input: a level-order tree, for example: [1, 2, 3, null, 4]
